System

Item definitions, instances, rarities and generated affixes

An authored item definition says what an item can be. An owned gear instance identifies one particular item; a stack row stores a quantity. A world pickup or resource node is a separate source, not the owned item itself.

Scope and player interaction

An authored item definition says what an item can be. An owned gear instance identifies one particular item; a stack row stores a quantity. A world pickup or resource node is a separate source, not the owned item itself.

StageMeaning
First integration: Phase05committed; full feature contract may include explicitly staged later extensions
EvidenceAuthored implementation specification; no native/Blueprint/backend runtime verified

UI state machine

DefinitionResolved → InstanceResolved → UnknownDefinition → Restricted → TooltipReady

WBP_ItemTooltip observes results from URPGItemCatalog. Pending is not Accepted. Close/cancel clears local focus and stale callbacks, but cannot undo an already committed backend command.

Definitions, fields and units

Canonical definition: URPGItemDefinition. Stable IDs, quantities, seconds and centimeters are validated by the owner, not inferred from translated labels or sprites.

Field / rule
ItemDefinitionId: stable item.* ID, content version and type family
OwnedItemId: server-generated UUID for nonstackable gear; immutable across bank/trade/zone moves
Rarity: Common|Uncommon|Rare|Epic|Legendary; authored/drop-generated, not UI color authority
ItemLevel and MinimumCharacterLevel: nonnegative integers; class/profession gates optional
MaxStack: positive integer for stackables; gear MaxStack=1
AffixDefinitionIds and rolled values: valid family/range only, rolled once on server
BindingPolicy: Unbound|BindOnPickup|BindOnEquip|AccountBound; owner restrictions
DurabilityCurrent/Maximum: bounded integers; set ID and weapon-hand requirement authored

C++ / Blueprint / backend ownership

LayerResponsibility
URPGItemCatalogImplement the native validated request/state lifecycle described below; native runtime state is not editable by UMG.
Blueprint/Data AssetsTune the declared defaults and visual/asset assignments. Keep definition references EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly; cosmetic hooks cannot grant rewards.
Zone serverValidate live actor ownership, range/LOS, alive/action state, cooldown/tool/target rules and current session epoch where relevant.
BackendFor durable changes, revalidate trusted catalog/revision/ownership and commit records/source claims/receipt atomically. Read-only/cosmetic features have no durable mutation.
WBP_ItemTooltipLocal observer/requester. Create only for local player; bind once, refresh immediately, unbind on teardown.

Custom command contracts

These names are project custom APIs or backend proposals, not existing Unreal/PaperZD nodes. Economic/backend requests are asynchronous; Pending resolves through the same command ID. Pure local queries are synchronous unless noted.

Command / result
ResolveItemDefinition(DefinitionId, ContentVersion) -> Definition|UnknownDefinition; read-only
GenerateOwnedItem(AuthorizedRewardSource, FamilyId, RollContext) -> ItemInstance|InvalidFamily; server/backend coordinated
ValidateItemUse(CharacterBuild, ItemInstance) -> Allowed|LevelRequired|ClassRequired|Bound
BuildTooltip(ReadOnlyItemView) -> LocalizedFields; presentation only

End-to-end command and observation flow

  1. Content author creates a definition with stable ID, type, stack policy, rarity, level requirements, price basis and optional visual mapping.
  2. A committed loot/craft/shop reward requests an item from an allowed family; server selects a permitted definition/affix outcome and records the resolved result in the command transaction.
  3. Generate one owned UUID for nonstackable gear and persist rolled properties; retries retrieve the stored result rather than rerolling.
  4. Inventory/equipment/bank/trade move the same instance identity and enforce binding/ownership without recreating it.
  5. UI resolves display text/icons/rarity styling from definitions and instance values; it does not compute a new random affix on hover.
  6. Unknown content version blocks unsafe mutation and shows an explicit unavailable-item view; migration maps old IDs without silently replacing rare items.

Editor configuration and real consumers

  1. Create native URPGItemDefinition from PrimaryDataAsset and the catalog resolver; expose authored fields EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly and validation errors.
  2. In Phase 05 define minimal backend item identity records for reward/transfer proof. Author the actual starter material/gear instances in Phase 09, not hundreds of unused shells in Phase 00.
  3. Create DA_Item_CopperOre, DA_Item_AshLog, DA_Item_RiverDace, DA_Item_HealingDraught, DA_Item_IronHatchet, DA_Item_TrainingSword, DA_Item_TrainingShield and DA_Item_WovenCloak as worked examples.
  4. Create WBP_ItemTooltip with name, type, rarity text, requirements, modifiers, binding, durability and comparison fields. Show stat-only equipment clearly when no visual overlay exists.
  5. Reopen catalogs and content validation: every referenced loot/recipe/vendor item ID must resolve before the zone enables that feature.

Reopen Phase05 integration entries after creating the assets. Test fixture: ServiceFixture_Items / Item_Gear_A / Item_Stack_Ore. No later-phase runtime dependency should be activated before its recorded integration phase.

Failure, contention and recovery acceptance

Test stimulus and expected result
Replaced item UUID in sell request -> ItemNotOwned or StaleItem; no sale of a different slot occupant.
Affix outside family/range -> InvalidAffix; content or request rejected.
Negative/overflow stack quantity -> InvalidQuantity; no arithmetic wrap.
Unknown definition after patch -> UnsupportedContentVersion and quarantine policy, not data deletion.

Repeat the success route with two clients when networking exists, then disconnect immediately before/after a committed result. Query the same command and compare authoritative snapshot/receipt with UI. Restart the relevant zone, reject stale epochs, and rerun the previous phase route. Pure visual/input features instead verify cleanup and unchanged server facts. These are future test recipes, not reported passes.

Tuning, accessibility and observability

Rarity weights, item levels, affix ranges and prices are proposals. No carry weight. Gear family can opt out of affixes entirely; deterministic starter gear is easier to test.

Ledger records item UUID, definition, source entitlement and affix result. Tooltips use text/icon distinctions as well as rarity color and support localization/long names.

Art gaps, production and do-not-build-yet

The asset ZIP and installed PaperZD APIs remain unverified. Required new art/unsupported layer combinations are tracked in art/animation-matrix.html and art/equipment-visual-matrix.html. A legal debug visual can prove authority but is not finished content. Production features listed as later/optional remain disabled until their phase/gate passes.
